We need to combine subnetworks into full network topology. We have two subnet topologies with resistor IDs overlapping (both have R1 etc). Need unique IDs across whole network. Also need to ensure connections between subnets: likely they share nodes A, X1, B etc. Subnet1: nodes A - N1 - N2 - X1. Subnet2: nodes B - N_b1 - (N_b2,N_b3,X1). So overall network includes both. Need to combine resistor lists, rename to avoid conflict. Could keep original IDs but they conflict; we can rename subnet2 resistors with prefix maybe R4 etc. Already note total resistors:7. Subnet1 has 3 resistors, subnet2 has 4 resistors =7. So keep IDs as given but they conflict: both have R1,R2,R3. Need to rename subnet2's resistors to R4,R5,R6,R7 maybe. Or rename to R4-R7 as they are 4 resistors. Let's map: subnet2 R1 (45) -> R4, R2 (10) -> R5, R3 (25) -> R6, R4 (5) -> R7. Then combine connections updating resistor IDs.

Subnet1 connections:
["A","N1","R1"]
["N1","N2","R2"]
["N2","X1","R3"]

Subnet2 connections with renamed:
["B","N_b1","R4"]
["N_b1","N_b2","R5"]
["N_b1","N_b3","R6"]
["N_b1","X1","R7"]

Now produce JSON with resistors dict of 7 entries.

Check measurements: they include many between nodes across subnets, e.g., A-B resistance 66.364 etc. Need to ensure topology matches measurements. Likely correct.

We could validate using simulate_circuit_resistance for some measurement to ensure consistency. Let's test A-B. Use tool simulate_circuit_resistance with combined topology and terminal nodes ["A","B"].
